In the given congruence, we have $a=95$ and $n=235$, and we're given that

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(95,235)=5.
$$

Since $b=50$ is divisible by $5,$ our congruence has $5$ solutions.

Next, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}95x & ≡50 &  & (\text{mod}\,235) \\ 5\cdot 19x & ≡5\cdot 10 &  & (\text{mod}\,5\cdot 47) \\ \cancel{5}\cdot 19x & ≡\cancel{5}\cdot 10 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{5}\cdot 47) \\ 19x & ≡10 &  & (\text{mod}\,47)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in this new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=19$ and ${n}_{1}=47$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(19,47)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $47.$

To find the solution, we must multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $19\,(\text{mod}\,47).$ To find the inverse of $19\,(\text{mod}\,47),$ we apply the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}47 & = & 19\cdot 2 & + & 9\, & ⇔ & \,9 & = & 47-19\cdot 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 19 & = & 9\cdot 2 & + & 1\, & ⇔ & \,1 & = & 19-9\cdot 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 9 & = & 9\cdot 1 & + & 0\, &  & \, &  & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, back-substituting in the usual way gives the following:

$$
1=5\cdot 19-2\cdot 47
$$

We can write this result in modulo $47,$ as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot 19-2\cdot 47 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,47) \\ 5\cdot 19 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,47)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse of $19$ modulo $47$ is $5.$

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $5,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}19x & ≡10 &  & (\text{mod}\,47) \\ 5\cdot 19x & ≡5\cdot 10 &  & (\text{mod}\,47) \\ x & ≡50 &  & (\text{mod}\,47) \\ x & ≡47\cdot 1+3 &  & (\text{mod}\,47) \\ x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,47)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡3\,(\text{mod}\,47).$

But our original congruence was modulo $235$ (not modulo $47$). To find all the solutions modulo $235,$ we repeatedly add $47$ to $3$ modulo $235$ until we reach the number $3$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,235) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡3+47≡50 &  & (\text{mod}\,235) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡50+47≡97 &  & (\text{mod}\,235) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡97+47≡144 &  & (\text{mod}\,235) \\ {x}_{5} & ≡144+47≡191 &  & (\text{mod}\,235) \\ {x}_{6} & ≡191+47≡238≡235+3≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,235)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1,2,3,4,5}≡3,\,50,\,97,\,144,\,191\,(\text{mod}\,235).
$$
